hero.title: Red Sea Global × Navier — silent, zero-emission island-hopping for a regenerative destination
hero.subtitle: An archipelago of luxury resorts needs guest mobility that matches the brand: fast, smooth, silent and clean. Foiling is the answer.
hero.what_we_do_together: We give The Red Sea and AMAALA a software-defined foiling fleet for guest island-hopping. Pioneer II glides silently between the hub and the resort islands with zero emissions over protected reef; Quanta-LR's hybrid range connects the destination to NEOM and the Jeddah gateway as single smooth legs. It is the on-water signature experience for a destination built around sustainability.

partner_context.their_ambition: You are building the world's most ambitious regenerative tourism destinations — The Red Sea and AMAALA — an archipelago of ultra-luxury resorts on a protected reef system, with a 100% renewable-energy, low-carbon promise at the core of your brand.
partner_context.their_pressure: Guest mobility across your dozens of islands must match that promise: silent, clean, gentle on the reef, and flawlessly premium. Diesel transfers undercut your entire proposition.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier is your on-water signature experience — software-defined foiling that glides silently between your islands with zero emissions over the reef, and Quanta-LR range to connect your destination to NEOM and Jeddah.

partner_json_extract.why_now: Red Sea Global is built on a regenerative, low-carbon promise across a sensitive marine environment — exactly where silent, zero-emission foiling belongs. Foiling lifts the hull clear of the water: smooth in chop, near-silent on approach, dramatically efficient, and gentle on reef. Pioneer II needs no charging infrastructure beyond a berth pedestal; Quanta-LR adds long-range hybrid reach with no infrastructure dependency. A ~100-vessel Navier network is already ramping in the Maldives (Bloomberg/WSJ, 2026) — the resort-archipelago playbook, ready to replicate.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time. A step-change in marine mobility, not an incremental faster boat.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open ocean and the berths and jetties already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way, no tunnels or tracks. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all. That's the fundamental contrast with flying taxis and other new-infrastructure modes: nothing to permit, build, or wait for.
why_navier_now.the_moment: Three forces just converged: the technology crossed from prototype to platform (10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out), decarbonization mandates turned legacy diesel fleets into stranded liabilities, and the hybrid removed the 'no charging at the islands' excuse. Autonomy is arriving on the water before the road. The marine layer is being claimed cluster-by-cluster right now.

partner_json_extract.multimodal_fit: The on-water layer of the guest journey — connecting the destination airport, the coastal hub and the resort islands into one silent, seamless arrival experience, then extending to NEOM and Jeddah.

differentiation.why_navier: Software-defined and autonomy-ready, a Turkey factory for supply, and — decisively — a ~100-vessel luxury-archipelago network already ramping in the Maldives: the exact playbook, ready to replicate on your reef.

proof_points.claim: The luxury-archipelago playbook is proven at scale.
proof_points.evidence: ~100 vessels / $100M / 3-year phasing in the Maldives — 'the playbook to replicate'.

proof_points.claim: The fleet model is real and at scale.
proof_points.evidence: ~100 vessels / $100M / 3-year phasing in the Maldives — the luxury-archipelago playbook proven commercially.

proof_points.claim: RSG is built for exactly this — clean, quiet, regenerative.
proof_points.evidence: The Red Sea is powered 100% by renewables with a regenerative-tourism mandate; a silent zero-emission foiling fleet is the native marine mode for it.

proof_points.claim: The destination scale demands a fast water network.
proof_points.evidence: 50+ resorts across an archipelago the size of Belgium, with Shura Island as the hub and AMAALA and NEOM beyond — distances only a foiling network covers quietly.

objections.concern: Is foiling gentle on the protected reef?
objections.response: Yes — the hull flies clear of the surface, so there is minimal wake, no diesel discharge, near-silent approach and zero emissions over sensitive water: the most reef-respectful powered mobility available.
Pioneer II covers intra-destination island hops; Quanta-LR (700 nm hybrid) connects The Red Sea↔AMAALA↔NEOM↔Jeddah with no charging-infrastructure dependency.

objections.concern: Can it run through the long, hot shoulder seasons?
objections.response: Climate-controlled cabins and far lower energy per mile suit Red Sea heat; the Quanta-LR hybrid carries the long inter-destination lines without any offshore charging dependency.

objections.concern: Does it preserve guest privacy and seclusion?
objections.response: Near-silent foiling arrivals, discreet direct resort-to-resort routing, and a premium charter tier keep the experience private — the opposite of a crowded public ferry.

the_ask.navier_brings: The software-defined foiling fleet (Pioneer II + Quanta-LR), the Maldives-proven luxury-archipelago playbook, captain training, certification and operations.
the_ask.partner_brings: You bring the destinations, the guest demand, the berths and the regenerative brand mandate.
the_ask.next_step: A resort-island shuttle pilot delivering the signature silent arrival experience.

close.title: Silent, clean island-hopping — worthy of the destination.
close.body: From a resort-island shuttle to a destination-wide network to the Saudi Red Sea luxury chain, Navier gives Red Sea Global the on-water signature experience its regenerative promise calls for — and the Maldives playbook proves it works.
